nodes.description: The frameshift replaces most of the native C terminus while preserving upstream DIX, PDZ and DEP domains. Transfected constructs produce detectable altered protein, but expression level, tag and host cell influence assay interpretation. The novel sequence has effects that differ from a simple stop construct.

nodes.description: The DVL1 subgroup in a small HR-pQCT study showed lower cortical and higher trabecular density, with fewer and thicker trabeculations. These are peripheral measurements and must not be presented as direct imaging of cranial bone or proof of uniformly increased skeletal density.

evidence.snippet: HR-pQCT revealed a unique pattern of low cortical BMD, increased trabecular BMD, decreased number of trabeculations, and increased thickness of the trabeculations for the DVL1-RS subjects.

nodes.description: DVL1 variants alter canonical and noncanonical WNT outputs. The 2015 C2C12 co-expression assay increased canonical activity, while 2023 HEK293 and fly assays supported reduced canonical output. JNK readouts increase for selected variants in HEK293 cells and in flies but are weaker in 2026 chicken facial cultures. These assays do not establish one direction in all patient tissues.

nodes.description: Cranial osteosclerosis was observed in four DVL1 cases in a seven-person mixed-genotype study and also in its single GPC4 case. It is enriched in DVL1-related Robinow syndrome but not demonstrated to be genotype-exclusive or universal. Neither altered nuclear DVL1 nor a canonical reporter effect has been shown to cause the human cranial bone phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Cranial osteosclerosis was only observed in DVL1-RS (4/4) and GPC4-RS (1/1) subjects and in one case was complicated by choanal atresia, bilateral conductive hearing loss, and cranial nerve III, VI, and VII palsy.

nodes.description: DVL1-related disease alters development of multiple craniofacial and oral structures. As one experimental component, chicken 1519ΔT misexpression widens the frontonasal mass and impairs prenasal cartilage and premaxillary bone formation, with reduced proliferation at the later embryonic time point. This model does not directly explain every human facial or oral feature, and neither increased proliferation nor impaired neural-crest migration was demonstrated as the cause.

nodes.description: Variant-expressing chicken cartilage is dysplastic, with irregular nuclei and patchy hypertrophic COL10A1 expression. Early Golgi-angle and cell-shape assays did not distinguish variants from wild-type DVL1 overexpression; only selected variant-versus-GFP comparisons were significant. Both wild type and variants shortened experimental bones. The specifically mesomelic human pattern is not fully explained.

nodes.description: Consider growth hormone replacement when endocrine evaluation demonstrates deficiency. A small 1999 clinical series reported increased growth velocity in treated patients, but their molecular subtypes were uncharacterized. This supports selected treatment of coexisting deficiency without establishing efficacy in DVL1-confirmed disease or correction of its developmental mechanism.

evidence.snippet: We propose its association with GH deficiency and that treatment with rhGH can result in a significant increase in the growth rate of these children.

nodes.description: Selected variants near the DVL1 C terminus cause a minus-one frameshift, replacing the native terminal sequence. Most are small coding insertions/deletions; c.1640-1C>T is a reported splice-acceptor variant with a predicted cryptic-splice/minus-one effect. A generic truncating variant elsewhere in the gene is not equivalent.

nodes.description: DVL1-variant misexpression in chicken limbs creates regions of virus-positive, SOX9-negative mesenchyme within cartilage. In the face, 1519ΔT replaces portions of SOX9-positive prenasal cartilage with TWIST-positive mesenchyme; later cultured cartilage expansion is impaired. These model observations support disturbed differentiation, without proving a patient-cell transcriptional target.

nodes.description: Tagged DVL1 frameshift proteins are more frequently nuclear in HEK293 cells. In the 2026 DVL-triple-knockout comparison, 1519ΔT is enriched in nuclei while wild type and the 1519-stop construct are mainly cytoplasmic. In Drosophila follicle cells, the human variants instead remain cytoplasmic/membrane-associated. Altered nuclear export or protein conformation is proposed; the exact export sequence and downstream transcriptional effects remain unresolved.
